sections.body: Two texts about the same topic can be very different. A diary of a sailor and an encyclopedia page about ships both tell you about the sea, but in different ways.
Compare: PURPOSE (to inform, entertain or persuade?), POINT OF VIEW (who is telling it?), and FACTS vs FEELINGS.
Use words like 'Both…', 'However…', 'In contrast…' to compare.
Read a news article and a story about the same animal. List one thing that's the same and one that's different.

quiz.q: A travel advert says a beach is 'paradise!'. A science article says the beach has 2 km of sand. What's the main difference?
options: The advert persuades; the article informs
hints: One wants you to visit. One gives facts.
A cereal advert says 'the tastiest cereal ever!'; a food label lists ingredients. Which persuades and which informs?
quiz.explain: The advert tries to persuade you; the science article gives information.

quiz.q: Which word helps show a DIFFERENCE between two texts?
hints: Two of these show things are the same.
'Cats are pets. In contrast, lions are wild.' 'In contrast' signals a difference. Which option does the same job?
